t: The first clause in section 1 of the Act of September 28, 1962 (76 Stat. 653), is amended by deleting the words “national wildlife refuges, game ranges,” and inserting therein “areas within the National Wildlife Refuge System,”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment substituting one phrase for another in an earlier Act. It does not establish any comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue; no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is a definitional or jurisdictional clarification within the federal government's own statutes.

opus.w: This section is a wording change. It replaces "national wildlife refuges, game ranges" with "areas within the National Wildlife Refuge System" in the 1962 Act. No one outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body or right to sue. The underlying Act's subject (managing wildlife refuge areas) doesn't make this amendment itself about participation.
opus.b: The tempting reading is to treat any amendment to a land-management statute as possibly involving participation. That fails here. The section only swaps one term for another: "national wildlife refuges, game ranges" becomes "areas within the National Wildlife Refuge System." It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the definition of "areas within the National Wildlife Refuge System" could implicitly affect public access or participation rights associated with those areas. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to participate in a decision.
